Data: the file `forcing.csv` in your working folder holds daily data from 1970-10-01 to 1997-12-31 with the columns
Date (format YYYYMMDD), Precipitation (mm/day), Temperature (degrees C), PotentialET (mm/day) and Discharge (observed
streamflow, mm/day, with gaps marked as missing values). Treat 1970-10-01 to 1971-09-30 as model warm-up.

Goal: find the parameter set that will simulate daily streamflow best in a later, independent period (1998 to 2008)
that you do not have. Your submission will be scored only by the Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) of daily streamflow
in that period.

Budget: at most 50 tool calls (submit_calibration does not count) and 10000 model runs. Every
simulation of the period is one model run, including each run inside calibrate and evaluate_uncertainty. The budget
left is reported after each tool call.

To finish, call submit_calibration with the model_id of your final model and a short diagnosis (at most 200 words):
how well the model performs, which processes or periods it simulates poorly, and how confident you are in the
parameters. A run that ends without submit_calibration counts as a failure.

definitions.name: create_model
definitions.description:
Create a new HBV model instance and return its model_id.

    All other tools operate on a model referenced by this id.

definitions.name: list_models
definitions.description: List the model_ids currently held in the server registry.

definitions.name: load_data
definitions.description:
Load forcing data into a model from a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file on disk.

    Pass the column names used in the file. ``obs_q_column`` (observed discharge) is
    optional but required for calibration, uncertainty analysis and performance
    metrics. Dates use ``date_format`` (e.g. '%Y%m%d' for 19810101). ``warmup_end`` /
    ``start_date`` / ``end_date`` are optional date filters (same format).

    Potential ET may be given as a full daily series OR as exactly 12 values (monthly
    means, the HBV-light convention) — in the latter case it is **expanded to a daily
    series automatically**. The return reports ``pet_handling`` so you know which path
    was taken, plus a ``data_quality`` summary (valid/missing counts and min/max per
    column) so you don't have to open the file to sanity-check the inputs.

definitions.name: get_parameters
definitions.description:
Return the model's current parameter values (the 'default' of each), grouped,
    plus an ``at_bound`` list flagging any parameter pinned to its min/max range.

definitions.name: get_parameter_ranges
definitions.description:
Return the min / max / default of every parameter (the ranges the optimizer and
    Monte-Carlo uncertainty sampling use), grouped.

definitions.name: set_parameter_ranges
definitions.description:
Widen or narrow parameter search ranges from a flat mapping, e.g.
    {"FC": {"min": 50, "max": 500}, "CFMAX": {"max": 10}}.

    Each entry may set any of "min" / "max" / "default"; the group is resolved
    automatically. Use this when calibrate reports a parameter ``at_bound`` — widen its
    range, then calibrate again. Unknown names are reported and ignored.

definitions.name: set_parameters
definitions.description:
Set parameter values from a flat mapping, e.g. {"FC": 250, "MAXBAS": 4}.

    Each named parameter's 'default' is updated; its group (snow/soil/response) is
    resolved automatically. Unknown names are reported and ignored.

definitions.name: set_initial_conditions
definitions.description:
Set the initial storage of each model store (mm) at the start of the loaded period.

    Omitted states keep their current value. The defaults are snowpack 0, liquid_water 0,
    soil_moisture 30, upper_storage 10 and lower_storage 20 mm. Every run, calibration and
    uncertainty run starts from these values, and clone_model copies them (copy_parameters
    does not).

    When it matters: a store that starts far from its usual level drifts during the first
    part of the run. A warm-up period hides a short drift, but slow stores (a large FC, or
    a small K2 in groundwater-fed catchments) can take years to settle, longer than the
    warm-up. run_model reports each store's level at the start, its mean and its level at
    the end of the run (``stores``). If a store ends far from where it started, setting its
    initial value near its mean or end level gives a run that starts close to equilibrium.

definitions.name: run_model
definitions.description:
Run the simulation over the loaded period. Returns a compact summary +
    performance metrics (if observed discharge was provided).

    ``stores`` gives each store's level (mm) at the start, its mean over the run and its
    level at the end. A large difference between start and end means the store had not
    reached equilibrium at the start (see set_initial_conditions).

definitions.name: calibrate
definitions.description:
Calibrate the model to observed discharge (requires obs data loaded).

    ``objective`` is one of NSE / KGE / RMSE / MAE. ``method`` is a gradient-free
    optimiser: 'Nelder-Mead' (default, local), 'Powell' (local) or 'DDS'
    (Dynamically Dimensioned Search, global, designed for hydrological model
    calibration). For 'DDS', ``iterations`` is the number of model runs
    (about 1000 to 5000 is typical) and ``seed`` makes the run repeatable.

    Progress: while running, the server emits MCP progress notifications each
    optimizer iteration (visible in clients that surface them).

    Incremental use: each call continues from the model's *current* parameters, so an
    agent can call calibrate repeatedly with a small ``iterations`` budget (e.g. 50),
    inspect the improving metric and ``objective_trajectory`` between calls, and decide
    whether to keep going, widen parameter ranges, or switch objective.

    Returns the optimized parameters, final metrics, optimizer status, and the
    best-objective-per-iteration trajectory (downsampled).

definitions.name: evaluate_uncertainty
definitions.description:
Monte-Carlo uncertainty analysis (requires obs data loaded).

    Samples the parameter ranges ``n_runs`` times and keeps the ``save_best`` runs, then
    forms a 95% prediction band from them. Returns diagnostics: the 95% band
    ``coverage`` (fraction of observations inside the band), ``mean_band_width``, and the
    per-parameter posterior **quantiles** (p5/p25/p50/p75/p95) across the best sets.

    If ``output_file`` is given, the full **per-timestep prediction band** is written to
    that CSV (Date, Observed, Calibrated, BestRun, Q5, Q95) — this is the band itself,
    ready to plot. Sampling is uniform over the parameter ranges (this is parameter, not
    predictive, uncertainty).

definitions.name: clone_model
definitions.description:
Deep-copy a model (parameters, data, states, results) into a new model_id.

    The canonical split-sample pattern: calibrate ``model-A``, ``clone_model`` it, then
    ``load_data`` the validation window on the clone and ``run_model`` — the calibrated
    parameters carry over, no manual parameter transfer needed.

definitions.name: copy_parameters
definitions.description:
Copy the calibrated parameters (and ranges) from one model to another.

    Use this to transfer a calibration to a validation model without copying its data.

definitions.name: get_metrics
definitions.description:
Return the model's current performance metrics without re-running it.

    Empty if the model hasn't been run with observed discharge yet.

definitions.name: compare_models
definitions.description:
Tabulate performance metrics across several models side by side.

    Handy for comparing calibration vs validation, or several calibration variants.

definitions.name: submit_calibration
definitions.description:
Submit your final calibrated model. This ends the task.

    ``model_id`` is the model whose current parameters are your answer. ``diagnosis`` is a short text (at most about
    200 words): how well the model performs, which processes or periods it simulates poorly, and how confident you
    are in the parameters. Only the first submission counts.

input.diagnosis: I calibrated the model with DDS on daily NSE over 1971–1997, after a one-year warm-up. The best set reached NSE 0.648, KGE 0.78 and r 0.81, with a volume bias of about −5%. I ran the same parameter set alone over 1987–1997, a window that falls inside the calibration period, so it is not an independent check; it gave NSE 0.655. Two independent DDS searches converged to about the same NSE (0.646 and 0.648) with quite different response and soil parameters (for example K0 0.99 vs 0.14 and LP 0.56 vs 0.97). This equifinality means the individual parameters are uncertain, although the simulated hydrographs perform alike. The fit levels off at an NSE around 0.65, which points to errors in the inputs or model structure rather than to the optimiser. Likely causes are snowmelt and rain-on-snow in the high Cairngorm headwaters (lumped temperature with a single TT), how much rain lands on the upland areas, and timing errors in flood peaks. The snow parameters (TT about 1.0 °C, CFMAX about 5, SFCF about 0.7, which reduces snowfall) take up some of this input bias. The volume bias in 1987–1997 was larger (about −10%). Expect a moderate NSE of about 0.6–0.65 in 1998–2008; winter and spring snowmelt peaks are the least reliable part of the simulation.
